subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics, Stage 5
syllabus: NSW Mathematics K-10 Syllabus (2022), Stage 5 core

points.title: Wages and salaries
points.brief: A wage is paid by the hour and a salary is a set amount a year. Converting between weekly, fortnightly and yearly pay, using 52 weeks in a year.

points.title: Overtime, commission and piecework
points.brief: Overtime is paid at a higher rate, such as time-and-a-half (1.5 times the normal rate). Commission is a percentage of sales, and piecework pays per item made.

points.title: Simple interest
points.brief: Simple interest is the same amount each period, worked out from the principal, the rate and the time with I = Prn. Making sure the rate and time use the same period.

points.title: Spending, GST and best buys
points.brief: Working out the cost of a purchase with discounts and GST, comparing prices by unit cost, and the cost of buying on credit or with a loan.

points.title: Compound interest by repeated percentages
points.brief: With compound interest, each period's interest is added to the balance, so the next period earns interest on interest. Multiplying by 1 plus the rate once for each period.

points.title: The compound interest formula
points.brief: The final amount is A = P(1 + r)ⁿ, with the rate and number of periods matched to how often interest is added. The interest is A minus P.

points.title: Depreciation
points.brief: Depreciation is an item losing value over time at a set rate. The value after n periods is the starting value times (1 - r)ⁿ.

points.title: Adding and subtracting algebraic fractions
points.brief: Fractions with pronumerals in the numerator and numbers in the denominator are added like number fractions, using a common denominator, such as x/3 + x/4 = 7x/12.

points.title: Multiplying and dividing algebraic fractions
points.brief: Multiply numerators and denominators, cancelling common factors first. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal.

points.title: Expanding and collecting like terms
points.brief: Expanding more than one set of brackets, such as 3(x + 2) - 2(x - 5), then collecting like terms, taking care with a negative outside the brackets.

points.title: Index laws with pronumerals
points.brief: Using the index laws on terms with pronumerals and coefficients, such as 3a²b × 4a³ = 12a⁵b and (2x³)² = 4x⁶.

points.title: Negative indices with numbers
points.brief: A negative index means the reciprocal, so 2⁻³ = 1/2³ = 1/8. Writing numbers with negative indices as fractions and back.

points.title: Three-step equations
points.brief: Solving equations that need up to three inverse operations, including ones with brackets, such as 2(x + 3) - 4 = 12.

points.title: Pronumerals on both sides
points.brief: Move the pronumeral terms to one side by adding or subtracting the same term on both sides, then solve, such as 5x - 3 = 2x + 9.

points.title: Equations with a fraction
points.brief: Multiply both sides by the denominator to clear the fraction, then solve, such as (x + 4)/3 = 5.

points.title: Equations from word problems
points.brief: Choosing a pronumeral for the unknown, writing an equation from the words, solving it and checking the answer makes sense.

points.title: Substituting into formulas
points.brief: Putting known values into a formula, such as v = u + at, then solving the equation that results for the unknown value.

points.title: Scientific notation
points.brief: A number in scientific notation is a number from 1 to less than 10 times a power of 10, such as 4.6 × 10⁵ or 3.2 × 10⁻⁴. Converting to and from ordinary numbers.

points.title: Very large and very small units
points.brief: Prefixes such as mega, giga, milli, micro and nano name powers of 10, used for distances in space or the size of cells and computer storage.

points.title: Significant figures
points.brief: Rounding to a number of significant figures, counting from the first non-zero digit, and knowing when zeros count.

points.title: Absolute and percentage error
points.brief: The absolute error of a measurement is half the smallest unit on the instrument. Percentage error is the absolute error over the measurement, times 100.

points.title: Gradient of an interval
points.brief: Gradient is rise over run. Positive gradients slope up to the right, negative slope down, horizontal lines have gradient 0 and vertical lines have no gradient.

points.title: Midpoint of an interval
points.brief: The midpoint is halfway between the two ends, found by averaging the x values and averaging the y values.

points.title: Distance between two points
points.brief: Draw a right-angled triangle with the interval as its hypotenuse, find the horizontal and vertical sides, then use Pythagoras' theorem.

points.title: Horizontal and vertical lines
points.brief: A horizontal line has an equation y = c and a vertical line x = c. Parallel lines have the same gradient.

points.title: Gradient-intercept form
points.brief: In y = mx + c, m is the gradient and c is the y-intercept. Reading both from an equation and drawing the line from them.

points.title: Finding the equation of a line
points.brief: Finding m and c from a graph, or from the gradient and one point, and writing the equation as y = mx + c.

points.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
points.brief: Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to -1, so a line with gradient 2 is perpendicular to one with gradient -1/2.

points.title: Graphs of parabolas
points.brief: The graph of y = ax² + c is a parabola. a sets which way it opens and how wide it is, and c moves it up or down.

points.title: Features of a parabola
points.brief: The vertex, the axis of symmetry and the x- and y-intercepts, and reading each from a graph or a table of values.

points.title: Exponential graphs
points.brief: In y = 2ˣ, y doubles each time x goes up by 1. The curve passes through (0, 1) and gets close to the x-axis without reaching it.

points.title: Exponential growth and decay
points.brief: Growth multiplies by a number greater than 1 each step, such as a population, and decay by a number between 0 and 1, such as a cooling drink.

points.title: Linear, quadratic or exponential
points.brief: Telling the three kinds apart from a graph, a table or an equation, such as equal differences in y for linear and equal ratios for exponential.

points.title: Naming the sides of a right-angled triangle
points.brief: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. The opposite and adjacent sides depend on which angle is being used.

points.title: Sine, cosine and tangent
points.brief: For a given angle, sin is opposite over hypotenuse, cos is adjacent over hypotenuse and tan is opposite over adjacent, the same for every triangle with that angle.

points.title: Finding a side with trigonometry
points.brief: Choose the ratio that links the known side and the unknown side to the angle, then solve, noting whether the unknown is on the top or bottom of the fraction.

points.title: Finding an angle with trigonometry
points.brief: Choose the ratio from the two known sides, then use the inverse function on a calculator, such as tan⁻¹, with the calculator in degree mode.

points.title: Angles of elevation and depression
points.brief: An angle of elevation is measured up from the horizontal and an angle of depression down from the horizontal. The two are equal as alternate angles.

points.title: Compass and true bearings
points.brief: A compass bearing such as S40°E starts from north or south. A true bearing is three digits measured clockwise from north, such as 140°.

points.title: Solving bearing problems
points.brief: Drawing a diagram from bearings, finding the right-angled triangle, and using trigonometry or Pythagoras' theorem to find a distance or a direction.

points.title: Composite areas
points.brief: Finding the area of a shape made of rectangles, triangles, trapeziums and parts of circles by adding or subtracting the simpler areas.

points.title: Surface area of a prism
points.brief: The surface area is the total area of every face. Drawing the net helps make sure no face is missed or counted twice.

points.title: Surface area of a cylinder
points.brief: A closed cylinder has two circles and a curved surface that unrolls into a rectangle of length 2πr, giving 2πr² + 2πrh. An open cylinder has one circle.

points.title: Volume of composite solids
points.brief: Splitting a solid into prisms and cylinders, finding each volume and adding them, or subtracting a hole that has been cut out.

points.title: Similar figures and scale factor
points.brief: Similar figures have the same shape, with equal matching angles and matching sides in the same ratio. The scale factor is how many times bigger one is.

points.title: Finding sides in similar figures
points.brief: Matching the corresponding sides, finding the scale factor from a known pair, then multiplying or dividing to find an unknown side.

points.title: Scale drawings and maps
points.brief: A scale such as 1 to 50,000 means 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm, or 500 m, in real life. Converting between map and real distances.

points.title: Quartiles and interquartile range
points.brief: Quartiles split ordered data into four equal parts. The interquartile range is the upper quartile minus the lower quartile, the spread of the middle half.

points.title: The five-number summary and box plots
points.brief: The minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum, and drawing them as a box plot.

points.title: Comparing datasets with box plots
points.brief: Placing box plots side by side to compare medians and spreads, and deciding which group did better or is more consistent.

points.title: Standard deviation
points.brief: Standard deviation measures how far values typically are from the mean. A small standard deviation means the data is clustered, found with a calculator.

points.title: Independent and dependent variables
points.brief: Bivariate data has two numerical variables. The independent variable goes on the horizontal axis and the dependent variable, which may depend on it, on the vertical axis.

points.title: Scatter plots and correlation
points.brief: A scatter plot shows each pair as a point. Describing the pattern as positive or negative, strong or weak, or no correlation.

points.title: Lines of best fit
points.brief: Drawing a line of best fit by eye, with about as many points above as below, and using it to make predictions inside the data with care beyond it.

points.title: Correlation and cause
points.brief: Two variables can be strongly related without one causing the other, as a third factor may drive both. Judging claims made from bivariate data.

points.title: Tree diagrams and tables of outcomes
points.brief: Listing the outcomes of two or more steps, such as tossing a coin then rolling a die, with a tree diagram or a two-way table of outcomes.

points.title: Independent and dependent events
points.brief: Events are independent when one does not change the chance of the other, such as drawing with replacement. Without replacement, the second draw depends on the first.

points.title: Multiplying along branches
points.brief: The probability of a path through a tree diagram is the product of the probabilities on its branches. Add the paths that give the event.

points.title: Simulations
points.brief: A simulation uses coins, dice, random numbers or a spreadsheet to model a chance situation, and many trials give an estimate of the probability.
